description: Backend self-reporting: make the two invisible clean-empty causes in the model-enumeration load path visible, and add a dedicated `provider_diagnostics` Tauri command that reports, per configured provider row, exactly what happened (kind, display-safe base_url, whether an instance was built, model count, and enumeration error). This is the backend data source for the visible diagnostics panel (FEAT-002) and the fix for the invisible-skip bug. This feature is the dependency for FEAT-002 (frontend consumes the new command + type) but is otherwise self-contained on the Rust side.
steps: INVISIBLE-SKIP FIX in crates/providers/src/builtins.rs `list_available_models`: the loop currently does `let Some(instance) = registry.get(&cfg.id) else { continue };` which silently drops a configured row whose instance was never built (contributes neither a model nor an error - a prime clean-empty cause). Change the None branch to push a ProviderEnumerationError { provider_id: cfg.id.clone(), message: <display-safe reason, e.g. "provider is configured but no instance was built (build failed or was skipped); it cannot be enumerated"> } into errors_out instead of `continue`-ing silently. Keep the message a static/display-safe string (no secret material). Update the function's doc comment (the paragraph describing the skip) to state the None case is now recorded as an error, not swallowed.

ADD a regression test in the builtins.rs `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: a config row referencing an id that has NO built instance in the registry now yields exactly one ProviderEnumerationError with that provider_id and a non-empty display-safe message, and models stays empty. Follow the existing FakeProvider/config test pattern (e.g. `instances_without_a_config_row_are_skipped` is the mirror image - add the new-direction case). Also assert the serialized error is camelCase (providerId/message) and contains no apiKey/secret substrings, mirroring the existing display-safe assertions.

REVIEW build_registry / ProviderRegistry::build_all short-circuit (crates/providers/src/registry.rs): build_all currently returns on the FIRST build_from_config error via `?`, so one un-buildable config row aborts the ENTIRE registry build (which becomes a thrown CommandError in list_available_models_inner - the frontend then sees a rejected promise). Decide and implement the least-invasive fix that keeps per-provider isolation: do NOT change build_all's existing signature/behavior used elsewhere; instead, in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs `list_available_models_inner`, replace the single `providers::build_registry(configs.iter(), ...)?` call with a resilient build that (a) starts from providers::builtin_registry(), (b) iterates configs building each via registry.build_from_config(cfg, secret_store), and (c) on a per-row build error, does NOT abort - it collects the row id so the enumeration path can report it. Because providers::list_available_models already reports any config row lacking a built instance as an error (from the invisible-skip fix above), simply skipping the failed build_from_config (not inserting an instance) is sufficient to surface it as a per-provider error rather than a whole-list abort. Add a code comment explaining this replaces the fail-fast build_registry to preserve per-provider isolation. If providers::build_registry then becomes unused in tauri-app, ensure no unused-import/dead-code clippy warning results (it is still used/tested in the providers crate, so only the tauri-app call site changes; verify no now-unused `use` remains).

ADD the `provider_diagnostics` command in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs following the established #[tauri::command] + `_inner` testability pattern (mirror list_available_models / list_available_models_inner). Define a display-safe serde boundary struct `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct ProviderDiagnostic { pub id: String, pub kind: ProviderKind, pub base_url: Option<String>, pub instance_built: bool, pub model_count: usize, pub error: Option<String> }` and a wrapper `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] pub struct ProviderDiagnosticsReport { pub configured_count: usize, pub total_model_count: usize, pub provider_count_with_models: usize, pub providers: Vec<ProviderDiagnostic> }`. NEVER include api_key_ref or any secret; base_url is the display-safe persisted string (or None). The _inner body must mirror list_available_models_inner's setup EXACTLY so it reports the SAME reality the picker sees: call ensure_ollama_provider_config(state) then ensure_embedded_provider_config(state) if list_available_models_inner does (check the current inner body and match its seeding calls precisely), load ProviderRepo::list, load AppConfig pricing, build the registry resiliently (per-row build_from_config as in the previous step) tracking which rows built, insert the shared EmbeddedProvider::from_shared instance (matching list_available_models_inner), then for each configured row: record kind, base_url, instance_built (registry.get(&cfg.id).is_some()), and call the instance's list_models() to get model_count / capture the display-safe error string on failure. Reuse providers::list_available_models's per-row logic conceptually but produce the richer per-provider report; keep it DISPLAY-SAFE (only ProviderError Display strings, never secrets).
REGISTER `provider_diagnostics` in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs generate_handler! list (add `commands::provider_diagnostics,` alongside `commands::list_available_models,`).

ADD Rust unit tests for provider_diagnostics_inner in commands.rs tests module (mirror the ensure_ollama_provider_config_is_idempotent / list_available_models_inner test setup that builds an AppState with an in-memory Db + InMemorySecretStore). Cover: (a) with no user config, the report includes the auto-seeded ollama-local row (kind Ollama, base_url None or the display default, instance_built true) and, since no live Ollama exists in the sandbox, its list_models errors so error is Some(..) and model_count 0 - assert the row is PRESENT with instance_built true and a non-empty error (the exact clean-empty diagnosis the user needs); (b) configured_count reflects the seeded rows; (c) the serialized report is camelCase and carries no apiKey/secret substrings (display-safe). Follow the existing async #[tokio::test] pattern in that tests module.

SELF-AUDIT the Rust changes for clippy -D warnings: no unused imports (adding ProviderKind/serde usage - confirm ProviderKind is already imported in commands.rs, it is via orchestrator_core), no needless borrows, no useless_vec, doc comments use flat prose (no indented list continuations that trip doc_lazy_continuation). Run `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` (fmt is the one gate runnable offline). Note in findings which checks were offline-verified vs. deferred to CI.
acceptance_criteria: providers::list_available_models records a ProviderEnumerationError (not a silent continue) for any configured provider row that has no built instance; a new unit test proves models stays empty AND errors has exactly one display-safe camelCase entry for that provider id.

list_available_models_inner no longer aborts the whole enumeration when a single provider row fails to build; a per-row build failure surfaces as a per-provider error via the enumeration path instead of a thrown CommandError.

A new `provider_diagnostics` #[tauri::command] exists, is registered in generate_handler!, has an _inner testable body, and returns a display-safe ProviderDiagnosticsReport with per-provider {id, kind, baseUrl, instanceBuilt, modelCount, error} plus configuredCount / totalModelCount.
provider_diagnostics_inner mirrors list_available_models_inner's exact seeding + registry-build + embedded-shared-instance setup, so it reports the same reality the picker sees.

Rust unit tests for provider_diagnostics_inner pass in CI: they assert the auto-seeded ollama-local row is present with instanceBuilt true and (in the sandbox/CI with no live Ollama) a non-empty error and modelCount 0, and that the serialized report is camelCase and secret-free.
cargo fmt --check passes offline for the tauri-app and providers crates; no obvious clippy -D warnings by review.
verification: Offline: `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` from hybrid-orchestrator/ both report no diff.

CI (deferred, orchestrator drives): `cargo build/test/clippy --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings` and same for crates/tauri-app pass, including the new provider_diagnostics tests and the invisible-skip regression test.
findings:
Implemented the backend self-report for the two invisible clean-empty causes plus the new provider_diagnostics command.

Files touched:
- crates/providers/src/builtins.rs: list_available_models's `let Some(instance) = registry.get(&cfg.id) else { continue };` now pushes a display-safe ProviderEnumerationError (static message 'provider is configured but no instance was built (build failed or was skipped); it cannot be enumerated') instead of silently continuing. Updated the function doc comment (flat prose) to state the None case is recorded, not swallowed. Added regression test `a_config_row_without_a_built_instance_is_recorded_as_an_error` (mirror of the existing instances_without_a_config_row_are_skipped): a config row with no built instance yields exactly one camelCase display-safe error and models stays empty; asserts providerId/message present and no apiKey/secret substrings.
- crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs: replaced the fail-fast `providers::build_registry(configs.iter(), ...)?` in list_available_models_inner with a resilient per-row build (builtin_registry() then build_from_config per cfg, ignoring per-row errors) so one bad row no longer aborts the whole enumeration; the unbuilt row now surfaces via the builtins invisible-skip fix as a per-provider enumeration error rather than a thrown CommandError. Added a code comment explaining why build_registry's short-circuit is intentionally not used here. Added the ProviderDiagnostic and ProviderDiagnosticsReport display-safe serde camelCase structs (id, kind, baseUrl, instanceBuilt, modelCount, error / configuredCount, totalModelCount, providerCountWithModels, providers) and the provider_diagnostics #[tauri::command] + provider_diagnostics_inner testable body. The _inner mirrors list_available_models_inner EXACTLY: ensure_ollama_provider_config only (it does NOT call ensure_embedded_provider_config), ProviderRepo::list, AppConfig pricing load, resilient per-row registry build, then insert the shared EmbeddedProvider::from_shared instance, then per-row list_models() for counts. DISPLAY-SAFE: only ids/kind/base_url/counts and ProviderError Display strings; never resolves secrets for the return value. Added two tokio tests: provider_diagnostics_inner_reports_seeded_ollama_row (seeded ollama-local present, kind Ollama, baseUrl None, instanceBuilt true, modelCount 0, non-empty error since no live Ollama; configuredCount == providers.len(); totals 0; serialized report camelCase and secret-free) and provider_diagnostics_inner_reports_unbuildable_row (a persisted GenericOpenAI row with no base_url fails to build, so instanceBuilt false with a display-safe error, other rows still reported).
- crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs: registered commands::provider_diagnostics in generate_handler! next to list_available_models.

Deviations/notes: build_all / build_registry in the providers crate are intentionally left unchanged (still used/tested there); only the tauri-app call site changed, and no now-unused `use` resulted (build_registry was always fully-qualified). Did not touch the Ollama IPv4 default or cloud-registration logic. Did not touch the embedded engine feature-flagging/bundle. Kept the requested `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]` on the two boundary structs exactly as specified.

Verified OFFLINE: `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/providers/Cargo.toml --check` and `cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check` both report no diff (exit 0). Cargo.lock unchanged (no new deps). Self-audited for clippy -D warnings: no unused imports (ProviderKind via orchestrator_core already imported; providers::builtin_registry/build_from_config used), no needless borrows/useless_vec, doc comments are flat prose (no doc_lazy_continuation). DEFERRED to CI (network-restricted sandbox, crates.io 403): cargo build/test/clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings for crates/providers and crates/tauri-app, including the new provider_diagnostics tests and the invisible-skip regression test.

HARDENING REFACTOR (review 2026-09-09-185504 Issue #1, drift risk): provider_diagnostics_inner previously re-implemented the picker's per-row get-instance/list_models/count-or-error loop INLINE, duplicating logic including the verbatim 'provider is configured but no instance was built ...' message that already lives in the shared providers::list_available_models (the `list_models` alias). That let diagnostics silently drift from what the picker sees. Refactored provider_diagnostics_inner (crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs) so, after the identical resilient registry build + shared EmbeddedProvider::from_shared insert, it calls the shared list_models(&registry, &configs, &pricing) ONCE and DERIVES each ProviderDiagnostic from the returned AvailableModelsResult { models, errors } plus configs: model_count = count of result.models whose provider_id == cfg.id; error = message of any result.errors entry whose provider_id == cfg.id (else None); instance_built = registry.get(&cfg.id).is_some(); total_model_count = result.models.len(); provider_count_with_models = count of configs with model_count > 0; configured_count = configs.len(). This removes the duplicated inline enumeration loop and the duplicated error-message string, so diagnostics structurally cannot diverge from the picker's per-row outcome. The now-loaded pricing (was `_pricing`) is passed into the shared call (stays used). ProviderDiagnostic / ProviderDiagnosticsReport struct shapes and serde camelCase field names are unchanged. Both existing provider_diagnostics_inner tests (seeded ollama-local row: instanceBuilt true, modelCount 0, non-empty offline error; unbuildable GenericOpenAI row: instanceBuilt false with display-safe error, other rows present) pass UNCHANGED because the shared fn records each failing/unbuilt row's error under the same provider_id (invisible-skip fix) and attributes models by provider_id, so the derived observable fields are identical. list_available_models_inner, builtins.rs, registry.rs, lib.rs, and all frontend files were NOT touched; no deps added; Ollama default and cloud logic unchanged. Removed an em dash from a code comment. OFFLINE-verified: cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check reports no diff (exit 0). DEFERRED to CI: cargo build/test/clippy -D warnings (crates.io 403 offline).
